The '''2011 FA Community Shield''' (also known as '''The FA Community Shield sponsored by [[McDonald's]]''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 89th [[FA Community Shield]], an annual [[association football|football]] match contested by the winners of the previous season's [[Premier League]] and [[FA Cup]] competitions. The match was the 160th [[Manchester derby]] between [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] and played at [[Wembley Stadium]], [[London]], on 7 August 2011.<ref>{{cite web |title=The FA Community Shield 2011 |url=http://www.wembleystadium.com/Events/2011/The-FA-Community-Shield-2011/The-FA-Community-Shield-2011 |publisher=Wembley Stadium |access-date=9 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202173645/http://www.wembleystadium.com/Events/2011/The-FA-Community-Shield-2011/The-FA-Community-Shield-2011 |archive-date=2 February 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Manchester United won the game 3–2, with goals from [[Chris Smalling]] and [[Nani (footballer)|Nani]] (2), after [[Joleon Lescott]] and [[Edin Džeko]] had put City 2–0 up at half-time.<ref name="BBC-Bevan">{{cite news |first=Chris |last=Bevan |title=Man City 2–3 Man Utd |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14420151 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2011 |access-date=8 August 2011 }}</ref>

Manchester United qualified to take part for the fifth consecutive year by winning the [[2010–11 Premier League]] title and Manchester City qualified by winning the [[2010–11 FA Cup]]. United won the match for the fourth time in five years.
{{TOCleft}}
{{-}}

==Background==
[[File:2011 Community Shield Teams.jpg|thumb|The two teams lining up for the [[God Save the King|national anthem]]]]
This was only the second occasion the two teams had met in the competition, with the first being the [[1956 FA Charity Shield]], which United won 1–0. Both teams secured their place in the 2011 Community Shield on the same day, 14 May 2011, when United clinched the [[2010–11 Premier League]] title with a 1–1 draw against [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] at [[Ewood Park]] and City beating [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] 1–0 a few hours later in the [[2011 FA Cup final]].
{{-}}
